newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea says would fire official seeking asylum.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea says would fire official seeking asylum.

text.p: North Korea said on Monday that it would dismiss a top Pyongyang official now in the South Korean embassy in China if he sought asylum.

The official KCNA news agency, monitored in Tokyo, quoted the Foreign Ministry as saying that if he had been kidnapped, then North Korea would take "decisive countermeasures," but "if he sought asylum it means that he is a renegade and he is dismissed".
The official, Hwang Jang-yop, was a top adviser to North Korea's supreme leader Kim Jong-il and was the highest-ranking official ever to defect from the Stalinist country.
Hwang has been staying at the South Korean mission in Beijing since last week. North Korea had previously suggested that Hwang was kidnapped, an allegation dismissed by South Korea.
The warning came in a brief KCNA item in which the foreign ministry was quoted as saying:
"Our stand is simple and clear. If he was kidnapped, we cannot tolerate (it) and we will take decisive countermeasures.
"If he sought asylum, it means that he is a renegade and he is dismissed."
